To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) positive mental health is associated with better professional beliefs and behaviors; (2) positive mental health may buffer some of the effects of burnout on professionalism, personal experience, and professional beliefs; and (3) medical student wellness programs should aim to prevent burnout, but should also promote mental health.

positive mental health is associated with reduced prevalence of suicidal ideation and serious thoughts of dropout, as well as improved professional behaviors and beliefs, and these associations persisted even in students with high burnout.
positive mental health is associated with lower prevalence of unprofessional behavior and higher levels of altruistic professional beliefs.

the impact of positive mental health on medical students’ professionalism in an era of high burnout.
the impact of positive mental health on the professional development and experience of medical students in an era of high burnout.
the impact of positive mental health on medical students’ professionalism.

medical students with positive mental health were more likely to be altruistic and less likely to be suicidal, to think of dropping out, or to engage in unprofessional behaviors.
